title: Anvil status JSON output (v1)
description: Wire shape emitted by `anvil status --json`. ADTRUST-005 pins this contract so editor extensions, CI hooks, and downstream tooling can consume the surface without pattern-matching against human-rendered output. Patch releases keep `schema_version` stable; minor releases bump it explicitly with a migration. Top-level objects accept additive optional fields (`additionalProperties: true`) so v1 stays compatible across patch versions; renamed or removed fields require a schema-version bump.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Consumers refuse any value other than `anvil.status.v1` and surface the mismatch as an upgrade hint rather than misinterpreting the document.

activation.description: Layered activation diagnostic. Field shape is driven by `crates/anvil-cli/src/activation/render.rs::render_json` and stays compatible across patch releases.

state.description: Single-word activation protection state from the `ProtectionState` closed set.

hooks.description: Discovered hook surfaces. Each entry names a file-mode or config-mode hook plus its active/inactive state.

recent_runs.description: Most recent gate runs from the on-disk cache. Truncated to a small number; ordered most-recent-first.

claim.description: MLP2-048: nested ProtectionClaim per spec §14. Closed-set vocabulary shared across every protection-rendering surface (status, MCP, doctor). Carries its own schema_version (anvil.protection-claim.v1) so consumers can pin against the claim contract independently of anvil.status.v1. Surfaces are empty in v1 of MLP2-048 because local CLI signals cannot enumerate per-surface state; IPC query_status integration will populate the array in a follow-up.

save_time_driver.description: DSV-049: the current worktree's headless save-time driver state from the daemon snapshot. Present only when a daemon answered AND the current worktree is registered, so consumers can distinguish 'no daemon evidence' (key omitted) from an explicit 'absent'. `unknown` is the forward-compat fallback a consumer surfaces for a driver state emitted by a newer daemon; treat it fail-safe as 'absent' (no attachment evidence). Additive-optional under `additionalProperties: true`; a renamed or removed value requires a schema-version bump.
